title: Choose u and change the limits
text: Let $$u=cos(theta)$$, so $$du=-sin\left(\theta\right) d\left(\theta\right)$$. The limits become $$u=1$$ and $$u=\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}$$.

title: Evaluate
text: The integral becomes the integral of $$u^{\left(-4\right)}$$ from $$\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}$$ to $$1$$, which is $$\frac{1}{3} u^{\left(-3\right)}$$ evaluated from $$1$$ to $$\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}$$. This gives $$\frac{2\sqrt{2}-1}{3}$$.
